Mikhail Korneev

Department of Politics and International Relations, Reuben College

I am a DPhil candidate in Politics at the University of Oxford, affiliated with Reuben College. My research sits at the intersection of political economy and comparative politics, with a focus on democratic innovations.

I am supervised by Prof. Petra Schleiter and affiliated with the Department of Politics and International Relations.

Research

My DPhil thesis examines the impact of democratic innovations on the quality of governance in Europe, with a focus on participatory and deliberative tools. I draw on the methods from comparative politics and political economy to analyze the effects of these innovations on citizen engagement, policy responsiveness, and regime support. My work contributes to debates on democratic resilience and the future of democracy in an era of rising authoritarianism.

Working Paper | Pseudo-Democratic Innovations and Genuine Regime Support in Russia

The project uses quasi-experimental methods to examine the impact of citizen participation on political participation and regime support in Russian regions. Argument Paper (PDF).

Working Paper | Mayor Recalls as an Accountability Mechanism

The paper developes a formal model of mayoral recalls as an accountability mechanism and applies it to the case of German municipalities.

Co-Authored Publication (Research Assistant) | Democratic Societies and Business

This report for the European Commission develops a framework for business engagement for democracy and provides practical recommendations for companies and policymakers. Publication (URL).
